Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/149486 (3.12 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/0d28f5e46e151718972dfabd91205444d0037b6d), first released in CPython 3.12.14; see the advisory https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/4FU62L2M6RMMHT2QPGQNPEHHUND7CEX5/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-7774. Compared Lib/tarfile.py in the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.12 package in every published build on x86_64 and aarch64 (3.12.12-r0 to 3.12.16-r4) with the upstream CPython 3.12 releases; both architectures agree. 3.12.12-r0 to 3.12.13-r1 ship the unchanged upstream file, and 3.12.13-r2 to 3.12.13-r11 ship it with other tarfile backports; none of them has the fix. 3.12.13-r12 adds a backport of the fix to CPython 3.12.13, and every later build has it: in _get_filtered_attrs() a link member that resolves to the destination directory is refused, and a symlink's target is resolved from the directory that holds the link. 3.12.13-r13 keeps the backport, and 3.12.14-r1 to 3.12.15-r1 ship the upstream 3.12.14 or 3.12.15 file unchanged. 3.12.16 builds ship the upstream 3.12.16 file unchanged, where the destination-directory check takes the reworked upstream 3.12.16 form (a link member whose name normalises to the destination directory is refused). The range ends at 3.12.13-r12.

tarfile.data_filter could be bypassed with crafted link entries, including symlinks with empty or directory-like names, so later members of a malicious archive were written outside the extraction directory by tarfile.extractall(). Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/149486 (3.13 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/0478bd83d82b255e0f29f613367a59d261e7eaa2), first released in CPython 3.13.14; see the advisory https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/4FU62L2M6RMMHT2QPGQNPEHHUND7CEX5/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-7774. Compared Lib/tarfile.py in the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.13 package in every published build on x86_64 and aarch64 (3.13.12-r0 to 3.13.18-r4) with the upstream CPython releases; both architectures agree. 3.13.12-r0 to 3.13.13-r9 ship the unchanged upstream file for their CPython version, without the fix. 3.13.14-r0, the first build of CPython 3.13.14 (the version string in libpython3.13.so), and every later build have it in _get_filtered_attrs(): a link member that resolves to the destination directory is refused, and a symlink's target is resolved from the directory that holds the link. Later builds ship the upstream file for their version or that file with further tarfile backports, and keep both checks; from 3.13.18-r0 the destination-directory check takes the reworked upstream 3.13.18 form.

Every later build keeps both checks: 3.14.6-1 to 3.14.8-0 ship the upstream 3.14.6, 3.14.7 or 3.14.8 file, some with other backported tarfile changes. 3.14.10 builds ship the upstream 3.14.10 file unchanged, where the destination-directory check takes the reworked upstream form (a link member whose name normalises to the destination directory is refused). The range ends at 3.14.6-0.

tarfile.data_filter could be bypassed with crafted link entries, including symlinks with empty or directory-like names, so later members of a malicious archive were written outside the extraction directory by tarfile.extractall().
